title: Sometimes read_temp() returns a random error code. Tap the bug.
explain: If adc_ready() is false, status is never set. The function returns whatever was on the stack. Give every local a value on all paths. Set status first, for example to -EBUSY, and change it on success.

title: Host test of a log buffer. Sometimes the value is not changed, sometimes it crashes. Tap the bug.
explain: push_back can grow the vector. Then it moves all items to new memory, and last points to freed memory. Writing to it is undefined behavior. Take the reference after the last push_back, or use an index. On firmware, prefer a fixed-size buffer.

title: Frame checksum panics in the debug build on long frames. The release build does not. Tap the bug.
explain: sum() on u8 uses normal addition. In debug it panics on overflow. In release it wraps silently, so the behavior depends on the build profile. If you want a sum mod 256, say so with wrapping_add. If the value must be exact, use a wider type.

pr.title: Do not lose button events
pr.author: junior-dev
pr.body: A button press is sometimes ignored. I use an atomic exchange to read and clear the flag in one step. Cortex-M4 build.

explain: The old code had a gap between the read and the clear. If the ISR fired in that gap, the new event was erased. atomic_exchange reads the old value and writes false in one step, so no event is lost. On Cortex-M3/M4 it uses LDREX/STREX. M0 has no such instructions, so check your toolchain there. Approve.

pr.title: Use enum class for the mode byte
pr.author: junior-dev
pr.body: The host sends a mode byte. An enum class is safer than magic numbers.

explain: The host can send any byte, for example 7. The cast gives a Mode that has no case. Then duty_for runs to the end of a non-void function. This is undefined behavior in C++. Check the raw value when you parse it. Also return a safe value after the switch.

pr.title: Reject too long log lines
pr.author: junior-dev
pr.body: Long lines overflowed the log buffer. Now they are rejected.

explain: The new return exits while the mutex is still taken. The next caller waits forever, and the log task and every other task that logs deadlock. Every exit path must release the lock. Best: check the input before you take the lock.

title: What does this print?
explain: int8_t c = -1 is promoted to int, so it stays -1. The literal 0xFF is the int 255. So -1 == 255 is false: 0. The cast (uint8_t)c gives 255, which equals 255: 1. Compare bytes as the same type, for example uint8_t.

title: What does this print?
explain: add() returns a reference, but d is declared as a value (Counter d). So the line copies the object after two add() calls: d.n is 2 and c.n is 2. Then d.add() changes only the copy: d.n is 3. Write Counter &d to keep a reference.

title: Two LEDs in parallel share one resistor, from one 3.3 V GPIO. One LED is bright and the other is dim. Why, and what is the fix?
options: Vf is not equal for both LEDs. The one with lower Vf takes more current. Give each LED its own resistor
The GPIO is too slow. Add a capacitor
The resistor is too small. Use a bigger one for both LEDs
LEDs can not be in parallel with a resistor at 3.3 V
explain: Every LED has a slightly different forward voltage. In parallel, the voltage is the same, so the LED with lower Vf takes most of the current and the other one gets little. One resistor per LED sets each current. It also protects the GPIO pin from the sum of both currents.

title: Reviewing code with locks: 4 rules
bullets: Find every return, break and error path between take and give. Each one must release the lock.
Check the input before you take the lock. Then there is no early exit inside it.
Never block, wait for a queue or call unknown callbacks while you hold a lock.
In an ISR use the FromISR API. Never take a normal mutex there.
